descriptionChirho: A rock-cut chamber or cave used for burial of the dead, the primary sense of μνημεῖον in the Gospels and Acts. Used of Jesus's tomb (Mt 27:60, Mk 15:46, Lk 23:53, Jn 19:41-42), Lazarus's tomb (Jn 11:17, 11:31, 11:38), and tombs of the dead generally. S72509 (sg) and S72510 (pl) share identical translation signatures: eng 'tomb/tombs', spa 'sepulcro/tumbas', hin कब्र/कब्रों, arb قبر/قبور, kor 무덤/무덤들, swa 'kaburi/makaburi'. Pure number inflection with no semantic distinction.

A monument or memorial structure built to honor or commemorate the dead, distinct from a functional burial place. Used in Jesus's condemnation of the Pharisees who 'build the monuments of the prophets' (Lk 11:47). Multilingual evidence diverges from the 'tomb' cluster: eng 'monuments' (not 'tombs'), spa 'monumentos' (not 'sepulcros'), hin स्मारक ('memorial', distinct from कब्र 'grave'), arb مقابر (which can mean memorial tombs), kor 기념비들 ('commemorative monuments', entirely different from 무덤 'tomb'). Hindi स्मारक and Korean 기념비 clearly mark commemorative rather than funerary function.
